title: What if oxygen disappeared for 5 seconds? You're at a rooftop bar downtown when every oxygen atom on Earth vanishes. Everyone's ears pop at once. Every flame dies. The river is 89% oxygen, so it turns into hydrogen gas. Glass, concrete and the floor under your feet crumble to dust. Then the oxygen comes back… and the hydrogen is still there. Would you have held on? 👇 #whatif #pov #simulation #science #fyp
audio: original sound 'son original' by 'What if?' - instrumental/ambient music bed only, no voiceover; level ramps slightly (-30 dB RMS early to -21 dB from ~8 s), silence only in the last 0.8 s
title_pattern: 'What if [everyday element] disappeared for [tiny N] seconds?' + second-person POV placement ('You're at a rooftop bar downtown when...') + escalating consequence list in the caption + twist when it returns ('...and the hydrogen is still there') + engagement CTA question ('Would you have held on? 👇'). Hashtags signal format: #whatif #pov #simulation #science.

thumbnail.source: TikTok originCover = first frame of the video (no designed thumbnail)
thumbnail.composition: 9:16 low-poly 3D render. Back of a blonde woman leaning on a rooftop parapet, lower-right third; dense low-poly city skyline across the middle; pink-violet dusk sky with string-light bulbs and a wire in the top third. Title in the upper-middle, small HUD countdown at left mid-height.
thumbnail.text: Centered serif (Garamond-like) white 2-line title 'What if oxygen disappeared / for 5 seconds?'; left-aligned HUD: tiny tracked caps 'OXYGEN DISAPPEARS IN', large thin numerals '0:07.192', tiny caps 'AIR PRESSURE 14.7 PSI'.
thumbnail.colours: Muted dusk palette: lavender/mauve sky, warm beige/grey buildings with lit windows, dark grey parapet, brown deck; white text only. Calm, almost pastel - no red arrows or saturated hype colours.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Single small human seen from behind versus a huge city - viewer stands in her shoes (POV proxy). Calm everyday moment versus the ticking countdown implies imminent catastrophe.
thumbnail.why_it_works: The live millisecond countdown makes even the first frame feel like a clock running; the serene, beautiful rooftop sets up a 'before' state the viewer instinctively expects to be destroyed. The elegant serif + HUD reads as a premium 'simulation', different from loud meme what-ifs.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: (on-screen, no voice) 'What if oxygen disappeared for 5 seconds?' + HUD 'OXYGEN DISAPPEARS IN 0:06.725' counting down in real time; at 5 s: 'You are on a rooftop bar downtown.'
hook.verbatim_0_11s: What if oxygen disappeared for 5 seconds? / You are on a rooftop bar downtown. / [countdown hits zero, flips to OXYGEN RETURNS IN 0:04.976, fire pit flames vanish] / Everyone's ears pop at once.
hook.device: Question title + live countdown timer (ticking-clock suspense) that hits zero at ~8 s, delivering the first visible payoff (flames die, pressure -21%) within the first 10 s. Second-person POV placement ('You are...') with a calm, beautiful scene as the 'before'. The timer stays on screen the whole video as a persistent open loop ('OXYGEN RETURNS IN ...').

beats.summary: Title question over a serene dusk rooftop; woman at the parapet; HUD counts down 'OXYGEN DISAPPEARS IN' from 0:06.7 in real time.
'You are on a rooftop bar downtown.' Camera pans across the bar deck to people around a gas fire pit under string lights; countdown reaches 0:00.1.
Countdown flips to 'OXYGEN RETURNS IN 0:04.976' (time slows to ~1/9 real speed); fire-pit flames go out; pressure 14.7 -> 11.6 PSI (-21%). 'Everyone's ears pop at once.' People clutch their heads.
Whip pans across sky/brick building. 'Oxygen is 21% of the air.' explains the pressure drop.
Camera turns to the river and skyline. 'Every engine stops.' Scale widens from the bar to the city.
'The river is 89% oxygen.' -> 'It turns into hydrogen gas.' River whitens and boils into rising white clouds; HUD switches to 'HYDROGEN CLOUD 340 FT HIGH' and climbs.
'Glass and concrete are half oxygen.' -> 'So is the ground beneath you.' Woman grips the parapet and looks down; camera tilts over the edge; threat turns from the city to the viewer's footing.
HUD 'THE GROUND HAS DROPPED 1 FT' climbing; the rooftop deck dissolves into foam/dust, people topple, camera tumbles into a sepia dust world of skeletal crumbling skyscrapers and a bridge.
'For now, nothing can burn.' Slow drift over a sepia wasteland as the ground keeps dropping (16 -> 30 ft) - foreshadowing line.
'Then the oxygen comes back.' Timer runs out to 0:00.000; a bright spark/flash appears over the dust plain.
HUD becomes 'THE FIRE 686 ft ... 140 ft ... HERE' (distance-to-viewer countdown). 'The hydrogen is still here.' An orange fireball rolls toward camera with debris and engulfs the frame.
Hard cut to a tilted, dim view through a cracked lens; HUD 'HYDROGEN + OXYGEN = WATER'; water droplets form on the glass (hydrogen burned back into water). Fades to black.
Black end card repeating the title plus a closing fact: 'OXYGEN IS 21% OF THE AIR AND 46% OF THE ROCK UNDER YOUR FEET'. Loop-friendly (title matches frame 0).

pacing.note_wpm: No narration. 12 short italic serif caption lines (3-7 words each) appear one at a time, each held ~3-4 s with ~1-4 s caption-free gaps; effective reading rate ~49 wpm. The ticking HUD supplies the tempo instead of a voice.
pacing.note_shots: Essentially one continuous simulated camera ('single take') with whip pans/tilts as transitions; ffmpeg scene detection found only 2 hard cuts (55.3 s flash, 62.5 s cracked-lens). Visual change every ~1-3 s in the first 40 s, then long 5-6 s drifting holds in the sepia wasteland. New escalation every ~4-5 s; HUD sub-line metric changes at each phase (pressure -> hydrogen cloud height -> ground dropped -> fire distance -> equation).
pacing.time_dilation: Pre-event countdown runs real time (0-8 s); the 5 'sim seconds' of no oxygen are stretched over ~47 s (~9.4x slow motion), shown by the millisecond timer.
pacing.caption_style: Centered white italic serif (Garamond/Cormorant-like), ~30 px at 540 wide, at ~62% frame height, fade in/out, no box. HUD top-left at ~45% height: tiny letter-spaced sans caps label, large thin serif numerals, tiny caps metric line.
pacing.music_sfx: Original instrumental bed throughout, no VO; no silence until the final 0.8 s.

transcript_source: burned-in captions read visually from 1 fps frame crops; faster-whisper small (CPU) confirmed no speech
techniques_worth_copying: Persistent HUD countdown (label + big millisecond timer + metric line) that turns the whole video into a ticking clock and an open loop; switching the label at each phase ('DISAPPEARS IN' -> 'RETURNS IN' -> 'THE FIRE 686 ft' -> 'HERE').
Time dilation: real-time countdown to the event, then the short duration stretched ~9x so each millisecond gets a consequence.
Fact -> consequence caption pairs ('The river is 89% oxygen.' / 'It turns into hydrogen gas.'), each 3-7 words, with the visual doing the explaining.
Escalation by scale and proximity: ears -> engines -> river -> city -> the ground under YOU -> the fire coming at you.
Live counters rising in the HUD (hydrogen cloud height ft, ground dropped ft, fire distance ft) as quantitative escalation.
Calm-before / false-calm line ('For now, nothing can burn.') right before the twist; twist delivered as the thing returning, not leaving.
Second-person POV with a proxy character seen from behind; first frame = thumbnail = end card for a seamless loop.
Premium restrained look: muted dusk palette, serif typography, no voice, no emojis - reads as a 'simulation' rather than a meme.
End card restating the title plus a bonus fact (46% of the rock under your feet) to reward rewatch and drive comments; caption CTA 'Would you have held on? 👇'.

code_only_remake_needs.feasibility: Medium-high. The original is a low-poly 3D scene (likely Blender/Unity) with particles; a Remotion version should go 2.5D: layered SVG/Canvas parallax planes (skyline silhouettes with window grids, river band, park, rooftop deck, flat-shaded figures) with a virtual camera (pan/tilt/zoom transforms + motion blur) to fake the single-take camera.
components: HUD component: tracked-caps label, big thin-serif timer driven by a time-dilation curve (real-time then ~1/9 speed), metric line with animated counters (PSI, ft) and phase-based label swaps.
Caption component: centered italic serif lines with fade in/out, from a storyboard timeline.

Low-poly city generator in SVG: random rectangles with window-grid patterns, depth layers with atmospheric haze; ability to 'disintegrate' buildings into particles (break rects into small squares that drift/fall).
Particle systems on Canvas: rising hydrogen cloud puffs (soft blurred circles), dust/sparkle grain, debris chunks, fireball (expanding radial gradients + noise mask), embers.
Water: river band with animated noise that whitens and boils into cloud puffs.
Flat-shaded faceless people built from polygons (2-3 poses: leaning, hands on ears, falling).
Camera rig: whip-pan transitions (directional blur + translate), screen shake, Dutch tilt, tumble.
Colour grading: dusk lavender -> haze -> sepia -> orange flash -> dim brown; full-frame orange whiteout transition.
Cracked-glass overlay: procedural SVG spiderweb crack paths animated with stroke-dashoffset, plus water-droplet sprites.
End card: black with serif title + fact line.
Audio: royalty-free ambient/cinematic bed with a riser into the fire moment and a boom at 0:00.000; no TTS needed (or optional quiet VO).
code_only_remake_needs.hardest_parts: Convincing 3D-feeling camera moves through a city and the dissolve/disintegration effects; fireball volume. Keep to 2.5D layers and particles; lean on typography/HUD, which carry most of the format's identity and are trivial in code.
